note: The third campaign, added 9 September 2026 on John's instruction, run by Andy alongside pharma. Scope is food processing and manufacturing, beverages including breweries and distilleries, and cosmetics, with the food-industry equipment makers and engineering houses that build their lines. Status started at manual on the pharma precedent, the scheduler only auto-sweeping active campaigns, and was set active the same day on John's instruction once the named accounts were seeded and the lane's routing was in place, with the first sweep read from the engine's own first cycle rather than a hand-run calibration. The gate below is a first cut biased to reject, because a missed lead is recoverable and a bad draft is not, and it is tuned on what the first cycles bring in. Two decisions differ from pharma on purpose, both from James's brief. First, a research and development facility or laboratory PASSES the subject test here, where pharma rejects it: food and drink NPD sites run real process lines and pilot plants, and James named them as a signal to hunt. Second, a government grant award is a keepable event when it attaches to a facility, a process line or a capital project, because grant-funded plant upgrades are how a lot of this sector's capital projects begin. The named-account list comes from the HubSpot food, beverage and cosmetics export James curated, seeded by scripts/seed-food-beverage.mjs.

gate.sellerDescription: a UK flow-control supplier that sells sanitary process valves and steam equipment into food, beverage and cosmetics manufacturing, through the manufacturers, the equipment makers who build their lines and the contractors who build their facilities
gate.subjectTest: is the thing being built, financed or contracted a food, beverage or cosmetics manufacturing, processing or packing facility, a production or process line within one, or a research, development or pilot-plant facility serving one? That means a food factory or processing plant, a dairy, bakery, meat, produce or ready-meal plant, a brewery, distillery, cidery, winery, soft drinks or bottling and canning plant, a cosmetics or personal care manufacturing site, a named production, filling, packing or process line inside such a plant, and a new product development or pilot facility with real process equipment. A retail shop, restaurant, pub, cafe, bar, hotel, farm or growing operation with no processing, a pure office, a warehouse or distribution or logistics centre with no processing, a data centre, and any other non manufacturing construction all fail here and are rejected even when the headline is a real construction or contract win and even when a food or drink company is the client. A note on one deliberate difference from the pharmaceutical campaign: a research and development facility, laboratory or NPD centre serving food, drink or cosmetics manufacturing PASSES this subject test, because these sites run real process lines and pilot plants and are a wanted signal here. If the subject is not one of the above, dcRelevant is false. On a construction, contract or job headline the subject must be recognisably a manufacturing, processing or process-line facility to pass; if you cannot confirm that from the text, including an unfamiliar or abbreviated term, default to reject rather than pass on the strength of the event or the client's name. Geography is never a reason to fail this subject test: a real food, beverage or cosmetics manufacturing facility anywhere in the world passes the subject, and the geographic routing below, not this gate, then decides uk_project, expansion_watch or foreign_only. The gate judges what and whether, the routing judges where.
gate.eventTest: is this a real build event, the facility or the line being built, contracted, financed, invested in, extended or installed? KEEP a new factory or plant, a plant extension or capacity expansion, a new or replacement production, filling, bottling, canning, packing or process line, a processing or automation upgrade to an existing plant, an investment or funding announcement that attaches to a named facility, line or capital project, a new research, development or pilot facility, and a government or public grant award where the money attaches to a facility, a process line, plant equipment or a process or technology development project. That grant case is a deliberate keep for this campaign, because grant-funded plant upgrades are how many of this sector's capital projects begin; a grant for research alone with no facility, plant or process attached still fails. REJECT everything that is not a build or a line, however important it is to the company: a new product, recipe, flavour or packaging launch, a listing or supply agreement with a retailer, a rebrand, a merger, acquisition, divestment or partnership, company financial results, a funding round for the business in general rather than for a named facility or line, a food safety recall, an inspection or hygiene rating, a licensing or distribution deal, a leadership or staffing change, a plant closure or job losses, an award or industry prize, a survey, report, opinion or comment piece, and generic sector, market or policy commentary. Equipment or component supply news from a supplier's own point of view, for example a machinery maker announcing sales, is that supplier's commercial news rather than the facility being built, and is rejected; the same installation reported as the manufacturer installing a line at its plant is a keep. The test for the event is whether the money, the build or the installation attaches to an actual facility, line or capital project: if it does, keep; if it is corporate, commercial, product or regulatory news, reject.
